ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a Zener voltage regulator circuit: the power supply on the left is labeled Vsource = 15 V; the upper terminal of the power supply passes through a series resistor Rseries, with the resistance value labeled as 500 Ω; the upper node after the series resistor is simultaneously connected to the middle Zener diode branch and the right-side load resistor branch; the Zener diode is labeled Vz = 5.1 V, and its lower terminal is grounded; the right-side load resistor Rload is also connected from the same upper node to ground. The problem gives Rload = 910 Ω. Reasoning calculation: According to the method, assume the Zener diode is in the breakdown voltage regulation state, therefore the output node is clamped at 5.1 V. The series resistor current is Iseries = (15 - 5.1) / 500 = 9.9 / 500 = 0.0198 A = 19.8 mA. The load current is Iload = 5.1 / 910 = 0.005604 A = 5.604 mA. By node KCL, the Zener current Izener = Iseries - Iload = 19.8 - 5.604 = 14.196 mA, approximately 14.2 mA.

method.method_draft: First describe the image values and topology: Vs = 15 V, Rseries = 500 Ω, zener voltage Vz = 5.1 V, and Rload = 910 Ω in parallel with the zener. Assume the zener is in breakdown and clamps the output node at 5.1 V. Compute the current through the series resistor: (15 - 5.1)/500 A. Compute the load current: 5.1/910 A. Use KCL at the top node to find zener current as series current minus load current, then convert to mA, yielding about 14.2 mA.
